title: Andreev reflection in Reissner–Nordström spacetime: coulombic pair-breaking and the electromagnetic Clogston radius
task: Solve Bogoliubov–de Gennes equations covariantly for Andreev reflection in Reissner–Nordström spacetime and derive electromagnetic Clogston radius
key_results: Coulomb field of charged black hole shifts electrochemical potentials over coherence length ξ by δμ(r)=eQξ/r², analogous to Zeeman splitting; electromagnetic Clogston (EMC) radius defined where pair potential transitions; doubly modified BTK conductance combines redshift-rescaling with Q-dependent subgap plateau erosion; extremal limit shows gapless conductance at infinity for Π>1/√2
comments: Novel application of relativistic quantum transport to curved spacetime; technically sophisticated but confined to theoretical framework; physical realism questioned (charged neutron stars insufficient for observation; Reissner-Nordström metric idealized).

model_io.model: Covariant Bogoliubov–de Gennes equations on Reissner–Nordström background

hypotheses.hypothesis: Coulomb field of charged BH induces radial pair-breaking analogous to Clogston bound, defining EMC radius
hypotheses.result: Confirmed (theory): modified BTK conductance exhibits Π-dependent gapless phase at extremal limit

title: Excitonic landscape and quasi-type-I nature in Moiré supercells of Ti-based MXene-MoS2 van der Waals heterostructures
task: Characterize excitonic landscape and quasi-type-I optoelectronic nature of Ti-based MXene–MoS₂ van der Waals heterostructures via many-body perturbation theory
key_results: GW-BSE calculations reveal quasi-type-I character despite type-II band alignment; optical transitions dominated by bright intralayer excitons (MXene-confined); interlayer transitions effectively dark due to negligible wavefunction overlap; non-radiative charge separation remains feasible
comments: Advanced many-body methods essential for accurate description; strain-relaxed Moiré supercells correct for 1×1 artifacts; decoupling of bright optical transitions from charge transfer dynamics useful for device design.

model_io.model: Many-body perturbation theory (GW-BSE) on Moiré supercells

hypotheses.hypothesis: Type-II band alignment permits fast non-radiative charge separation, but interlayer exciton transitions are dark
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: GW-BSE shows bright optical transitions confined to MXene; interlayer wavefunction overlap negligible

title: Room-temperature alignment-free magnetometry with boron vacancies in hot-pressed hexagonal boron nitride
task: Enable alignment-free room-temperature magnetometry using boron vacancies in polycrystalline hot-pressed hexagonal boron nitride
key_results: Room-temperature ODMR from V_B⁻ in polycrystalline hBN enables scalar (alignment-free) magnetometry; ensemble orientation averaging preserves magnetic-field sensitivity while eliminating precise alignment requirement; numerical simulations (hyperfine, anisotropic broadening) accurately predict ODMR response
comments: Scalable platform leveraging disorder as advantage for practical quantum sensing; vector field reconstruction not possible, limiting some applications but enabling robust ambient operation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Random crystallite orientation enables alignment-free magnetometry while maintaining sensitivity
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: ensemble ODMR retains clear magnetic-field dependence without precise alignment

title: Metastable MnBi2Te4 enabled by magnetic-field-assisted synthesis
task: Transform antiferromagnetic to ferromagnetic ground state in MnBi2Te4 via magnetic-field-assisted synthesis
key_results: Field-grown MnBi2Te4 exhibits FM ground state with Tc~12.5 K (vs. AFM in conventional samples); de Haas-van Alphen oscillations confirm electronic property modification
comments: First-principles support validates field-induced spin reordering as design principle for magnetic topological insulators, though practical scalability of synthesis route unclear.
